newsitem.title: USA: Marvel bondholders will fight new plan.
newsitem.headline: Marvel bondholders will fight new plan.

text.p: The bondholder committee of Marvel Entertainment Group Inc plans to oppose a reorganization plan developed by Marvel and Toy Biz Inc, a spokesman for the committee said Monday.
"We will fight this plan vigorously with every legal remedy available under the bankruptcy laws," the spokesman said.
"Marvel's board is abdicating its responsiblity to their shareholders in favor of the banks and Toy Biz insiders with this proposed plan," said the spokesman.
He called the plan, disclosed by Marvel today, "a worse deal for stockholders" than a plan offered by Ronald Perlman and approved by Marvel's board last December.
"This plan dilutes the Marvel shareholders even more than the original plan," said a source close to Marvel bondholders.

Shareholders would receive only warrants to purchase up to 12.5 percent of the new company, while under the Perlman plan shareholders would have received a 20 percent direct equity stake in the new company, the source said.

A Marvel spokesman, asked to comment on the bondholder committee criticism, said, "Anybody is welcome to bid and make an offer for the company. If it is worth what the bondholders say it is worth, then Marvel will receive a bid to that effect and the bondholders will receive the recovery they want."
The Marvel spokesman declined further comment.
In a written statement issued today, Marvel said it would consider bids from other parties in an auction process.
Under the proposed reorganization, Toy Biz would be merged with Marvel's publishing and liscensing business.

Toy Biz shareholders would receive 72 percent of the new entity. Marvel's secured lenders would receive a 28 percent stake, proceeds of a new $250 million term loan and a five-year $170 million note from the new company, and Marvel's Fleet/Skybox and Panini subsidiaries.

A Marvel spokesman said Marvel and Toybiz officials are working to finalize details of the proposal. The final plan will be subject to approval by the bankruptcy court as well as the Marvel and Toybiz boards, he said.

Meanwhile, the bondholder committee plans to appeal a court ruling preventing committee members from voting their Marvel shares to oust Marvel's board. Oral arguments on the appeal are scheduled for Thursday, a committee spokesman said.
